titulo: Work, forms and formal e-mails: Formal and informal e-mails

aula.objetivo: Write formal and informal e-mails (greeting, subject, request, apology, closing), fill in forms, and understand job and course ads, at A2 writing level.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: a formal e-mail (to a company, to someone you don't know) opens with «Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,» (Dear Sir or Madam) — or «Sehr geehrte Frau Müller,» / «Sehr geehrter Herr Müller,» — and closes with «Mit freundlichen Grüßen» (Kind regards) and your name. Use «Sie» and polite forms. STEP 2: an informal e-mail (to a friend) opens with «Liebe Anna,» or «Lieber Paul,» and closes with «Liebe Grüße» or «Viele Grüße» (Best wishes). Use «du». STEP 3: the SUBJECT line (Betreff) is short: «Anfrage zum Deutschkurs» (Inquiry about the German course). STEP 4: the body goes: introduction, request, thanks: «Ich möchte mich für den Kurs anmelden. Könnten Sie mir bitte weitere Informationen schicken?» STEP 5: the polite request FORMULAS: «Könnten Sie mir bitte …?», «Ich würde gern …», «Ich bitte um …». STEP 6: replying: «Vielen Dank für Ihre Antwort» (Thank you for your reply). STEP 7: after the comma of the greeting, the first word of the e-mail starts in lowercase (unless it's a noun or «Sie»).
blocos.comparacao: English "Dear…" works for everyone; German splits it: «Sehr geehrte/r…» for formal e-mails and «Liebe/r…» for friends — and «Liebe/r» is NOT for your bank. "Sincerely" / "Kind regards" = «Mit freundlichen Grüßen».

erros.motivo: In a formal e-mail, the greeting is «Sehr geehrter/geehrte».
In German, the greeting is in German.

blocos.enunciado: Say out loud how you'd open and close a formal e-mail and an informal one.
Write 8 sentences about health and appointments: symptoms, instructions and requests.
